question: What recall does hybrid (0.7 semantic + 0.3 BM25) retrieval achieve on CUAD?
lesson: Established the 61.4% recall@3 baseline with EmbeddingGemma (35.2% with NLEmbedding). Embedding quality matters: a 26-point gap between embedders. This is the number every retrieval idea is measured against.

question: Which embedding model is best for on-device CUAD retrieval, and does an absence instruction help doc QA?
lesson: EmbeddingGemma beat the alternatives tested. A plain 'if not in the sections, say so' instruction improved contract QA faithfulness. Prefer EmbeddingGemma unless a new idea beats it on a measured recall basis.

question: How many chunks (top-K) should be retrieved for Qwen doc QA?
lesson: K=3 chunks is optimal; more chunks added distractors and hurt answer quality. Ideas that increase retrieved context should justify why they beat K=3.

question: Can BM25-only match hybrid recall while removing the 600MB embedding model?
lesson: BM25-only recall was ~15 points below hybrid on CUAD; semantic embeddings are necessary. Do NOT re-propose dropping semantic retrieval for pure lexical — it's settled.

question: Does prepending document/section context to chunks before embedding improve recall, like Anthropic's contextual embeddings?
lesson: Registered (pre-registration draft, 2026-10-19); NOT yet run, so there is no result. Pre-registration concern on record: the drafted approach is a naive static title/heading prepend, which does NOT match Anthropic's method (model-GENERATED per-chunk context + contextual BM25 + reranking) — verify the actual mechanism before treating the cited 35% gain as reachable. Don't re-propose naive-prepend contextual embeddings; the open question is the generated-context variant.

question: Is there a better semantic/BM25 weight than 0.7/0.3 for recall?
lesson: Swept semantic weight 0.1-0.9; recall rises monotonically to 58.1% at 0.9, +6.3 points over the 0.7 run, so ADOPTED a higher semantic weight. Caveats: the optimum sits at the edge of the tested range (retest >0.9 / pure-semantic before over-trusting 0.9); hard categories like Exclusivity (~11%) are weight-invariant, so weighting is not their bottleneck (chunking/question formulation is); and the 0.7 run here read 51.8% vs PoC-007's 61.4% baseline, so treat 013's absolute numbers as within-experiment. A plain 0.1-0.9 re-sweep is settled; extending the range or adaptive per-category weighting is still open.
